newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar firm as March wobbles above $300.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar firm as March wobbles above $300.

text.p: London's spot white sugar contract managed to teeter above its early $300 resistance point in modest turnover on Friday afternoon but traders said sellers would be quick to take profits from another upside assault.

Covering of short positions accounted for a lot of the market's firmness during the early part of the session when March hit $300 a tonne, touching off buy stops which briefly pushed it to $301.00, they said.
But sellers were quick to cap the gains and March continued to hover around $300 in a tight trading range of $1.40.
"I think most people are still short and just buying when they need to. They don't want to sell aggressively at these levels yet," said one trader.
Most sellers looking to take profits on the brief burst of strength would be operating on a scale-up basis, he said.
At 1620 GMT March was up 80 cents at $300.50 and May was up 80 cents at $300.00. Volume totalled 1,093 lots, the vast bulk of which came from the spot month.

Although March's break of resistance has pushed March through its 10-day moving average, the position still faces a swathe of technical barriers as its other shorter-term averages are closely arranged in parallel up to $304.50.
Elsewhere, the Czech state will buy up to 30,000 tonnes of sugar from the 1996 domestic surplus for its reserves.
Traders cited market talk that Pakistan had abandoned its tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar for end-December but more details have yet to emerge.
Nearby Paris positions were slightly firmer but overall volume was extremely thin at just 115 lots.
March and May were both up 40 cents, at $300.30 and $300.00 respectively.
